summary:
Confirmation re-review of 50e04c0~1..55baf04 (fix commit 50e04c0 + verifier test commit 55baf04). My original critical finding is RESOLVED and PROVEN in both trees: all 4 pending-challenge render blocks (received/sent x web/mobile) now render the @username sub-line in the correct slot - name/pseudonym line, then @username when present, then the timeLeft countdown - and the /api/challenge list payload does carry username on both sender and recipient, so the sub-line has real data. I did not take the handoff's word for it: I read all 4 blocks and then mutation-tested the new render tests in a throwaway git worktree (flipping `c.sender.username &&` / `c.recipient.username &&` to `false &&` turns 6 of 8 assertions red across both tree test files; deleting the `setResults([])` line from each search component's new else branch turns both failure-branch tests red). All 4 warnings and 3 minor findings are genuinely addressed in code, not just claimed: accept/decline routes now call climberDisplay with recipient.id (getChallenge/acceptChallenge both include userSelect which selects id, so the id is real - the narrow display_name-only select in challenge.ts belongs to reapExpiredChallenges, not these paths); app/tsconfig.json has "@app/*": ["./src/*"] and it is exercised for real (tests/components/mobilePendingChallengesIdentity.test.tsx imports @app/lib/handle AND pulls the mobile component that imports @app/* into the root TS program - `pnpm typecheck` passes, which is the direct refutation of the TS2307 I demonstrated last round); the triplicated gate is now one module, src/lib/userSearchQuery.ts, with three non-test callers (route, web UserSearch, mobile UserSearchSection) and zero leftover local isSearchable/EMAIL_SHAPE copies anywhere under app/src, app/app or app/mobile; both search UIs now clear results, set a shared searchFailureMessage() copy and render it with role="alert", suppressing the conflicting 'No user found' line; FriendsList uses Boolean(friend.user.username); the not.toContain("@") assertion is narrowed to the row's

lines; DuelHome's duplicated placeholder prop is gone and UserSearch's default string is byte-identical, so nothing changes on screen. Fresh pass over the whole delta found no new defect introduced by the fix commits: gates green (pnpm lint clean, pnpm typecheck clean, pnpm test 85 files / 799 passed in 8.81s vs 748 baseline - no perf regression), no dead code, no debug statements, no schema/dep change, error copy uses existing tokens. Three non-blocking notes below, all pre-existing or cosmetic: the challenge_expired cron notification is the last challenge-flow notification still naming a placeholder ('your opponent'), the search path still has no in-flight request sequencing so an out-of-order response can resurrect a stale row, and one test doc comment overstates searchFailureMessage's caller count. Verdict: APPROVED.
goal: Confirm the reviewer's prior critical finding (missing @username sub-line on the 4 pending-challenge rows, web + mobile) is actually fixed in both trees, spot-check that the 4 warnings and 3 minor findings were addressed rather than claimed, and do a fresh pass for anything newly introduced by the fix commits 50e04c0 and 55baf04.

findings.issue:
RESOLVED (was the critical finding). All four rows now render the handle in the correct order inside the existing min-w-0 column: primary line ({name} challenged you / Waiting for {name}), then {c.sender.username &&

@{username}

} (recipient.username on the sent rows), then the font-mono timeLeft countdown - the countdown was not displaced. Verified the data exists rather than assuming: app/app/api/challenge/route.ts:132-133,169-170 maps username onto both sender and recipient, and both components' ChallengeItem interfaces declare username: string | null on both. Web and mobile are byte-equivalent modulo each tree's className idiom (same commit, per context/conventions.md). Coverage is real and proven, not asserted: tests/components/pendingChallengesIdentity.test.tsx (4 cases) and mobilePendingChallengesIdentity.test.tsx drive the mounted components with a stubbed fetch, compare against the real imported climberHandle (no hardcoded pseudonyms), assert the countdown still renders, and assert the negative case (no username -> no line starting with '@'). Mutation proof in a scratch git worktree: replacing both gates with `false &&` in both files -> 6 failed / 2 passed. The scenario from my original finding (display_name null by default via ensureUser, no friendship required by createChallenge, so no Friends-List row to cross-reference) now renders 'Swift Ibex 42 challenged you' + '@bobsmith' + countdown.

RESOLVED (warning 1). Both sites now call climberDisplay(c.recipient.id, c.recipient.display_name) / climberDisplay(challengeBefore.recipient.id, challengeBefore.recipient.display_name); the `display_name ?? username ?? "Your opponent"` chains are gone and an app-wide grep for `?? username` and 'Your opponent' returns nothing in either challenge tree (the only surviving 'Your opponent' is app/app/api/duel/[id]/rematch/route.ts:73, the duel flow I already scoped out as a follow-up). Person named by climberDisplay is the right person in both: the accepter IS the recipient and the notification goes to sender_id; the decliner IS the recipient and the notification goes to sender_id. The id is genuinely present - I checked the DB layer rather than trusting my own earlier note: app/src/db/challenge.ts:22-23 userSelect selects id/display_name/username and is the include used by both acceptChallenge (line 132) and getChallenge (line 198). The narrow `sender: { select: { display_name: true } }` at challenge.ts:239-240 is reapExpiredChallenges' own select (cron), not these routes, so there is no undefined id reaching climberHandle. `pnpm typecheck` passing corroborates this.

RESOLVED (warning 2) and no longer dead config. "@app/*": ["./src/*"] sits alongside "@/*" with no baseUrl (paths resolve relative to the tsconfig) and `exclude` is untouched, so the default program scope is unchanged - resolution only. It is exercised on both toolchains: the mobile test imports `@app/lib/handle` directly AND imports ../../mobile/src/components/challenge/PendingChallengesSection, which imports @app/lib/handle and @app/lib/userSearchQuery, pulling the previously-unreachable mobile tree into the root TS program. `pnpm typecheck` (tsc --noEmit) exits 0, which directly refutes the TS2307 I reproduced last round, and tests/components/userSearchFailureBranch.test.tsx mounts the mobile UserSearchSection too. The mobile challenge tree now has both typecheck and render coverage.

RESOLVED (warning 3), and the extraction is a genuine move, not a copy. The route deleted its local EMAIL_SHAPE + exactMatchFilter and imports exactMatchFilter from the shared module; both search components deleted their byte-identical isSearchable + EMAIL_SHAPE and import isSearchableQuery/searchFailureMessage (web by relative path, mobile through @app/lib/userSearchQuery). A grep for `isSearchable(`, `EMAIL_SHAPE` and `normalizeUsername` across app/src, app/app and app/mobile shows no second copy left. isSearchableQuery is now literally `exactMatchFilter(q) !== null`, so client and server gate cannot drift by construction - the class of bug the duplication invited. The module keeps the WHY comments (exact-match-only because email is PII; usernames stored pre-normalised so normalising the query is what makes the lookup case-insensitive), stays Prisma-free via the structural UserSearchFilter union (correctly explained: the mobile bundle must not pull ORM types), and my earlier nit about the unnamed inline union and the belt-and-braces `norm.valid && norm.username` is addressed by the named type plus a one-line comment. Three non-test callers, each reachable from a rendered screen (duel page -> DuelHome -> UserSearch; mobile ChallengeScreen -> UserSearchSection; the route itself). tests/lib/userSearchQuery.test.ts adds direct unit tests including the reserved-name ('admin') reject case I asked for and the prefix/anti-enumeration invariant.

RESOLVED (warning 4). Both components now have the missing else branch: clear results, set searchFailureMessage(res.status), open/announce it; the catch does the same with status null instead of swallowing. Status-to-copy mapping lives once in the shared module (429 -> 'Too many searches. Try again in a little while.', null -> 'Network error. Try again.', else generic), so the two surfaces cannot disagree. Rendering is correct on the states that used to conflict: the error

carries role="alert" in both trees, uses the existing text-ember token, and the 'No user found...' line is now gated on !searchError so a failure can never read as an empty result. The debounce effect clears searchError on every query change, so the message does not outlive the query that caused it. Mobile's `void notifyError()` inside the try's else is safe - haptics.notifyError is internally try/caught and early-returns off-native, so it cannot throw into the catch and downgrade the 429 copy to the network copy (I checked mobile/src/lib/haptics.ts rather than assuming). The design-review error-state gap for these two components is closed. Mutation proof: deleting the `setResults([])` line from each else branch turns both userSearchFailureBranch tests red (the stale @creator-1 row and its Add button survive).

RESOLVED (all 3 minor findings). FriendsList uses `Boolean(friend.user.username)`, so all 6 sub-line gates are truthiness now. The fragile whole-subtree `not.toContain("@")` is replaced by an assertion on the row's

textContents (`lines` contains the real climberHandle, and no line starts with '@') - it now fails for the right reason only. DuelHome's duplicated `placeholder` prop is dropped and UserSearch's default is the byte-identical 'Search by email or username…' (same character, same ellipsis), so there is zero user-visible change and one copy-string.

Pre-existing, NOT introduced here, and non-blocking - but the new code comment overstates the guarantee. Both `search` callbacks have no AbortController and no in-flight request/sequence guard, so responses can land out of order. Concrete sequence: (1) type 'creator-1' -> debounce fires request A; (2) keep typing to 'creator-12' -> the effect clears searchError and searched, debounce fires request B; (3) B returns 429 first -> results cleared, error

shown; (4) A's slower 200 resolves -> setResults([creator-1]) + setOpen(true), and because the results

    is not gated on !searchError (UserSearch.tsx:174), the stale creator-1 row and its clickable Add button render UNDER the error message next to input text 'creator-12'. That is the same wrong-person click the else branch was added to prevent, just via reordering rather than via a missing branch. It also pre-dates this diff (two successful out-of-order responses always showed the older row), so the fix did not regress anything and this does not block merge - I am recording it because the new comment says 'Never leave the previous query's row ... on screen next to a different query', which is only true for in-order responses.
findings.fix: Follow-up, not this diff: track a request sequence id (or an AbortController stored in a ref) in both components and ignore/abort any response that is not the latest query's; then the comment is literally true. Cheap interim: gate the results <ul> on !searchError in the web component (mobile already renders results and error in separate blocks but has the same reordering hole).

findings.issue: Untouched by both commits and outside this diff, so non-blocking, but it is the last placeholder in the challenge notification flow and it is exactly the class of miss my earlier learning warned about (enumerate received/accepted/declined/EXPIRED before declaring a flow converted). challenge_expired still builds its body from `c.recipient.display_name ?? "your opponent"`, so after this change a sender sees 'Swift Ibex 42 challenged you' / '... accepted your challenge' / '... declined your challenge' and then 'Your challenge to your opponent expired' for the same person. Worth stating precisely because the fix is nearly free: reapExpiredChallenges already selects recipient_id (src/db/challenge.ts:238), so no select or type change is needed.
findings.fix: Follow-up ticket: `const recipientName = climberDisplay(c.recipient_id, c.recipient.display_name);` in the cron route. No schema change, no widening of ExpiredChallenge.

findings.issue: Doc-comment inaccuracy in an otherwise strong test file: it claims searchFailureMessage 'has three real callers (the route's 429 and both search UIs)'. The route does not import searchFailureMessage - it returns its own API envelope ({ error: 'Too many requests', code: 'RATE_LIMITED' }, 429), which is correct (machine-stable code for the wire, player-facing copy for the UI). Two callers, both clients. Also minor: EMAIL_SHAPE is exported but has no non-test importer (it is only used internally by exactMatchFilter and asserted directly by this test file's last describe) - fine as a documented constant, just noting it is export-for-test.
findings.fix: Optional: reword to 'two real callers (both search UIs); the route returns its own wire-level RATE_LIMITED envelope'. Do not add a route caller to make the comment true - the split is the right design.

findings.issue:
Fresh-pass result, recorded so qa-acceptance need not redo it. Nothing new and defective was introduced by the fix commits. Gates re-run from app/: `pnpm lint` (eslint --max-warnings=0) exits 0; `pnpm typecheck` (tsc --noEmit) exits 0 - notable because the diff widens the TS program to the mobile tree; `pnpm test` = 85 files / 799 tests passed in 8.81s against the 748-test baseline, i.e. +51 tests and no suite-runtime regression. Delta hygiene: no dead code (the route's normalizeUsername import went away with the function it fed), no console/debug statements added, no schema/migration/dependency change, no new magic values (STATUS_RATE_LIMITED is named), no scope creep - the only files touched outside the findings list are the 5 test files, tsconfig.json and loop/handoffs. Every changed control has a non-test caller: the 4 pending-challenge rows via DuelHome (app/duel/page.tsx) and mobile ChallengeScreen, the shared module via the route + both search components, the tsconfig alias via real production imports. Design-review pass on the changed components: error state added where it was missing, role="alert" on both new error

s, token-based colours only (text-ember / text-text-muted), sub-line uses `truncate` inside the existing min-w-0 column so a long handle cannot break either row's layout. I left the working tree clean - the mutation experiments ran in a `git worktree` under the scratchpad, which I removed (`git status --porcelain` empty).
findings.fix: None - informational. qa-acceptance: the automated tests now cover the display_name-null + username-set challenger on both trees, so the remaining manual value is the live 429 path (spend the 60/hr budget, then type a fresh query and confirm the previous row is gone) and the out-of-order-response case in the warning above.

learnings.insight: Mutation-testing a fix's new tests in a throwaway `git worktree` (with app/node_modules symlinked in) is a cheap, read-only way for a reviewer to prove a regression gate is real: worktree add <sha>, flip the exact line the fix added, run only the relevant vitest files, worktree remove. Here it converted 'the handoff says the sub-line is tested' into '6 of 8 assertions go red when the gate is flipped to false' and '2 of 2 go red when setResults([]) is deleted', in under a minute and with the real working tree untouched. This is the concrete answer to my own prior learning that 'verified by code reading' in a handoff is not evidence.
learnings.action: Reviewers re-reviewing a fix: before writing 'resolved', mutate the added line in a scratch worktree and confirm the new test fails. If it still passes, the test is asserting something else and the finding is not closed. Never mutate the real working tree.

learnings.insight: Extracting a triplicated predicate paid off beyond the duplication: making isSearchableQuery literally `exactMatchFilter(q) !== null` means the client gate and the server gate cannot drift, so 'the UI pre-check matches the API' stops being a comment claim maintained by hand across three files and becomes a property of the code. The mobile tree could join only because the same change added "@app/*": ["./src/*"] to app/tsconfig.json, and the structural UserSearchFilter union (no Prisma.UserWhereInput) is what keeps the ORM types out of the Capacitor bundle while the route still spreads the filter into its `where`.
learnings.action: When you find the same guard hand-mirrored in N files, prefer one exported predicate plus a Prisma-free structural return type over N synchronized copies - and check the shared module is importable from every tree (tsconfig paths + the bundler alias) in the same commit.

learnings.insight: Adding an error branch to a debounced search is only half the stale-row fix. Both search components still have no AbortController or request-sequence guard, so a slow success can land after a fast 429 and repaint the previous query's row - complete with its Add button - underneath the error message, next to different input text. The new comment ('Never leave the previous query's row on screen next to a different query') is therefore true only for in-order responses. Same shape as the challenge_expired notification: the flow was declared converted while one member of the set (expired) still names a placeholder.
learnings.action: When fixing 'stale UI after a failed request', add response sequencing (abort or latest-query id) in the same change, or scope the comment to what the code actually guarantees. When converting a notification flow, list every type in it (received/accepted/declined/expired) and tick them off - including cron-emitted ones, which no UI grep will surface.

learnings.insight: Re-review scope: 2 commits (50e04c0 fix + 55baf04 tests), 19 files, +1235/-72. Prior round's 8 findings all verified addressed in code (1 critical + 4 warnings + 3 minor), 0 new critical, 2 new non-blocking warnings (both pre-existing code outside the diff). Gates all green from app/: lint 0, typecheck 0, 85 files / 799 tests in 8.81s (baseline 748 tests - +51, no runtime regression). Three mutation experiments run in a scratch worktree, all three turned the intended tests red.
learnings.action: Orchestrator: route to qa-acceptance. The two new warnings are follow-up tickets (search response sequencing; challenge_expired cron naming), not loop-backs - neither is in the diff under review.
